newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain denies opposition claim it seized children.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain denies opposition claim it seized children.

text.p: Bahrain on Sunday denied an opposition claim that it had arrested 60 children in connection with political unrest in the Gulf Arab state.
"The claim is incorrect. It is completely baseless," a government official told Reuters.

The London-based Bahrain Freedom Movement said in a statement on Sunday that Bahrain -- scene of sporadic unrest over the last two years -- had arrested 60 children, most of them below 16 years of age.
In one incident, security forces stormed the house of Hussein Mohammad Ali in Sitra area, beat him up and seized his two sons, Mohammad and Amin -- both less than 10 years old, it said.

The movement also said Bahrain University professor Zahra Isa al-Zeirah was asked by the government to submit her resignation on January 20 "on grounds she expressed some ideas on the political situation in the country".
Her dismissal was part of disciplinary action against civil servants, school teachers and university professors, it added. There was no government confirmation.

Members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protests, arson attacks and violence since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms from the Sunni-led government.
At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds have been detained, including children, since the unrest began.
